newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania to propose Constanta for Caspian oil route.
newsitem.headline: Romania to propose Constanta for Caspian oil route.

text.p: Romanian Foreign Minister Adrian Severin on Tuesday proposed using the Black Sea port of Constanta and the Danube as the safest route for oil and gas from the Caspian Sea and ex-Soviet Central Asia into into Europe.

In an interview before leaving for talks in Italy and the United States, Severin said Romania's stability in the volatile Balkan region made it a logical choice for sending oil, using the Georgian port of Poti as a staging point for tankers.
"There are different routes for transporting natural gas and crude oil from Central Asia, the Caspian Sea and the Caucusus," he said.

"The need is crucial for Europe and consequently there is a need to assure the stability of these routes. Romania is one of the countries that can ensure that stability. We can keep open these routes."
Severin said he would raise the issue in talks next week with U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright as part of Romania's efforts to promote regional stability and win early membership of NATO.

A number of countries in the region have proposed using their territory for oil transit from Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan and other former Soviet republics to Europe, avoiding the volatile Caucasus region of southern Russia.
Ukraine has suggested sending oil from Poti to a terminal it is building near the port of Odessa. Bulgaria has proposed a route linking its port of Bourgas to Russia's Black Sea port Novorossiisk.
